data.name: SW-D001
data.value: This file is not a text configuration: it is most likely a backup encrypted with a password. Shiftwall never decrypts backups. Export the configuration again without encryption: in the GUI, click your user name (top right) > Configuration > Backup and leave "Encryption" disabled; in the CLI, use "execute backup config" without a backup password. Keep the exported file in a safe place.

data.name: SW-D002
data.value: This is a YAML-format backup. Shiftwall reads FortiOS-format backups only: export again choosing "FortiOS" as File format (GUI: user name > Configuration > Backup).

data.name: SW-D003
data.value: The "#config-version" header line is missing: model and firmware version cannot be read from the file.

data.name: SW-D004
data.value: This looks like a partial configuration ({0}). A full backup is needed for a migration.

data.name: SW-D005
data.value: Line {line}: private-data-encryption is enabled. Secrets (ENC values) are encrypted with this FortiGate's private key: the new FortiGate must use the same private-data-encryption key BEFORE the configuration is restored, otherwise those secrets cannot be decrypted. Since FortiOS 7.6.1 the key is generated randomly when the option is enabled, so plan to re-enter passwords and pre-shared keys if the key cannot be reproduced.

data.name: SW-D007
data.value: Line {line}: {0} password(s) are masked with "FortinetPasswordMask". Fortinet does not recommend restoring such a file: export a normal backup for the migration.

data.name: SW-D008
data.value: {0} encrypted value(s) (ENC) found. They are copied unchanged and never decrypted.
